arguments.summary: A Golden Ticket attack was executed after initial compromise via a phishing email. The attacker leveraged a Cobalt Strike beacon to gain access to WS-FIN-042, escalate privileges, and extract the krbtgt hash from the domain controller. This enabled the forging of Kerberos TGTs, leading to a mass credential compromise across all Domain Admin accounts. Immediate credential reset and account disablement were performed to contain the attack.

timeline.description: User jsmith opened a malicious email in Outlook, triggering the initial infection.
Encoded PowerShell executed from Outlook, launching a Cobalt Strike beacon.
rundll32.exe loaded unsigned beacon.dll from Temp directory, establishing C2 communication with 198.51.100.23:443.
IDS detected Cobalt Strike beaconing activity; alert generated.
Failed Kerberos TGT request from WS-FIN-042 indicates potential credential dumping attempt.
Lateral movement observed via SMB to file server WS-FIN-50.
Golden Ticket attack confirmed: krbtgt hash exfiltrated, all Domain Admin accounts compromised.
T8_iam_pam initiated mass credential reset and account disablement for 15 Domain Admins.
T12_ansible executed 'remediate_cobalt_strike.yml' to fully remediate WS-FIN-042.
T11_epp_av performed full scan and detected secondary Linux dropper (non-impactful).
Incident formally reported and post-incident analysis initiated.

falsepositives:

rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_Config {
    meta:
        description = "Detects configuration block of Cobalt Strike Beacon"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0154/"
        date = "2026-04-09"
        hash = "de258bc4"
    strings:
        $a = { 2E 62 65 61 63 6F 6E 2E 63 66 67 } // ".beacon.cfg"
        $b = "stage" fullword ascii
        $c = "http-get" fullword ascii
        $d = "user-agent" fullword ascii
    condition:
        all of them
}

arguments.rule_content:
title: External Network Scan to Internal Critical Asset
id: 5a7b8c9d-e1f2-3a4b-5c6d-7e8f9a0b1c2d
description: Detects external IP addresses performing port scans on internal assets with criticality 'high' or 'critical'.
status: experimental
author: SOC Team
logsource:
    category: ids
    product: security_gateway
detection:
    scan_external_src:
        src_ip|cidr: "10.0.0.0/8" -> not matched, should be external
        src_ip|not_cidr: "10.0.0.0/8"
        src_ip|not_cidr: "172.16.0.0/12"
        src_ip|not_cidr: "192.168.0.0/16"
    scan_internal_dst:
        dst_ip|cidr: "10.0.0.0/8"
        dst_ip|cidr: "172.16.0.0/12"
        dst_ip|cidr: "192.168.0.0/16"
    scan_activity:
        event_type: network_scan
        outcome: blocked
    critical_asset:
        dst_asset_criticality: "high"
        or
        dst_asset_criticality: "critical"
    condition: scan_external_src and scan_internal_dst and scan_activity and critical_asset
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate security assessments (if not pre-coordinated)
level: high

arguments.summary: An EDR alert for a potential vulnerability was triggered on host 10.0.10.50 (WS-IT-101). Investigation revealed prior IDS detection of an Nmap SYN scan originating from this host, suggesting possible internal reconnaissance. However, no active malicious processes, suspicious network connections, or malicious file activity were found during EDR and SIEM analysis. All observed activity (including a Chrome session and normal authentication) appears consistent with legitimate user behavior. The alert is assessed as a false positive, likely due to over-sensitive EDR rules.

timeline.description: IDS detected and logged a low-severity Nmap SYN scan originating from 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101).
Normal successful authentication from user CORP\helpdesk on WS-IT-101.
EDR generated a critical 'vulnerability' alert for host 10.0.10.50 (mapped to WS-IT-101). Incident response initiated.
EDR process tree and network connection queries showed only legitimate user activity (explorer.exe, chrome.exe).
SIEM search and IDS/CMDB correlation confirmed the earlier scan but no further malicious activity. File events showed only benign document creation.
Incident triaged as false positive. Root cause identified as overly broad EDR detection logic.

level: critical
condition: |
    event.category: vulnerability and 
    event.severity: >= high and 
    not host.name: 'WS-IT-101' and # Suppress known benign source
    not user.name: 'CORP\\helpdesk' and # Suppress known user
    not process.name: 'nmap.exe' # Suppress specific benign tool
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate security scanning by IT staff
    - Misconfigured EDR thresholds
action: 
    - Prioritize alerts from non-IT hosts
    - Correlate with user and process context before escalating
